title: Dispatch: tracked head count and derived reaction allowance (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6`, including its acceptance criteria — they include closing the reactionAllowance write path). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR); your branch already contains migrations through 0035 — the next contiguous number is 0036. This child has an IMPORTER part and an ENGINE part. Read AGENTS.md (incl. "Deterministic rules-pack importer work"), docs/importer-fix-protocol.md, docs/rules-pack-compiler.md, docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5, ADR 0020 §§2-3. The SRD freeze guard is dormant: never touch freeze-manifest.json hashes or add thaw notes.

SOURCE (creature:hydra). Multiple Heads: "The hydra has five heads. While it has more than one head, the hydra has advantage on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, and knocked unconscious. Whenever the hydra takes 25 or more damage in a single turn, one of its heads dies. If all its heads die, the hydra dies. At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each of its heads that died since its last turn, unless it has taken fire damage since its last turn. The hydra regains 10 hit points for each head regrown in this way." Reactive Heads: "For each head the hydra has beyond one, it gets an extra reaction that can be used only for opportunity attacks." (already typed: extraReactions formula one-per-head-beyond-one, restrictedTo opportunity-attacks). Multiattack: "as many bite attacks as it has heads" (attack counting stays model-adjudicated by the accepted F2 design — do not automate it).

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
IMPORTER
1. Add a typed curated mechanic to the Multiple Heads trait through the compiler's curated-spec technique (find where creature trait mechanics such as extraReactions are curated, and the kindSchemas.ts effect validators): { kind: 'multipleHeads', initialHeads: 5, headDiesWhenDamageInOneTurnAtLeast: 25, headsRegrownPerDeadHead: 2, regrowthSuppressedByDamageType: 'fire', hitPointsPerRegrownHead: 10, deathWhenNoHeads: true }. Every value is source-backed; record the source span/provenance the way sibling curated mechanics do. Register the field in kindSchemas validation. Regenerate the pack through the importer workflow (committed output must equal regenerated output); review the generated diff: only creature:hydra's Multiple Heads mechanics (plus derived ledgers that legitimately carry it) may change. Search the pack for any other creature with a "heads" mechanic of the same shape; only add the mechanic where the source states it.
ENGINE (generic over the typed mechanic, never keyed on 'creature:hydra')
2. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0036_combatant_heads.sql: encounter_combatant gains head_count INTEGER NULL CHECK (>= 0), heads_died_since_own_turn INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, fire_damage_since_own_turn INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK IN (0,1), damage_this_turn INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, damage_turn_key TEXT NULL (identifies the turn the accumulator belongs to, e.g. combat instance + round + acting participant from the action-economy turn state), head_died_this_turn INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. ADR 0015 conventions; regenerate the schema snapshot; document in schema.ts.
3. start_encounter initializes head_count = initialHeads for a combatant whose rules record carries multipleHeads.
4. update_combatant gains `damageTypes?: string[]` (the damage types of a negative hpDelta, declared from the resolve_damage result — a declared input). On damage to a multi-head combatant: add to damage_this_turn for the current turn key (reset when the turn key changes); the first time in a turn the accumulated damage reaches the threshold, one head dies (at most one head per turn); set fire flag when 'fire' is among damageTypes; head_count 0 → status dead (concentration/actor sync via the normal path).
5. At the end of the multi-head combatant's own turn (begin_turn of the next participant implicitly ends it — find that seam in actionEconomy.ts beginTurn), if heads died since its last turn and no fire damage since its last turn: head_count += regrown (2 per dead head) and heal 10 per regrown head (clamped to max; through the combatant HP path; not if dead). Then reset heads_died_since_own_turn and fire_damage_since_own_turn. Report the regrowth in begin_turn's result.
6. Reaction allowance is DERIVED: for a combatant whose record carries extraReactions formula 'one-per-head-beyond-one', allowance = max(1, head_count) (1 + heads beyond one) whenever the budget row is created or head_count changes; restriction clause unchanged. REMOVE reactionAllowance from update_combatant's schema and run path (a supplied value is now rejected as an unknown arg by schema validation); replace setReactionAllowance's public use with the derivation (keep an internal function only if the derivation uses it). Update the actionEconomy.ts over-budget rejection hint, the update_combatant description, the Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, and module comments: the extra reactions now come from the tracked head count; never compute them.
7. Expose head_count in the combatant roster/context rendering and the update_combatant/begin_turn results so the DM sees it (advantage on listed saves while heads > 1 and the Multiattack count stay DM interpretation).
8. A5 bookkeeping: design doc A5 "Existing contracts" paragraph — record that the reactionAllowance contract is restored on a derived path (eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6). Tests in tools.test.ts / protocol.test.ts / actionEconomy.test.ts that assert the downgrade disclosure must be replaced by assertions on the derived contract (and the old actionEconomy case driving update_combatant reactionAllowance to success replaced by a tool-registry test proving the input is rejected).

TESTS: importer projection test for the curated mechanic (values + provenance) and kindSchemas validation; engine: init 5 heads; 24 damage no death, 25 accumulated across two hits in one turn kills one head, at most one per turn; next turn resets; fire suppresses regrowth; regrowth +2 per dead head and +10 HP each; all heads dead → dead; reaction allowance tracks heads (5 → 5 reactions, extras restricted to opportunity attacks); reactionAllowance arg rejected; a creature without the mechanic unaffected.

OUT OF SCOPE: Multiattack automation; advantage automation; anything not listed.

TEST COVERAGE IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE: write every test listed under TESTS (one `it` per bullet at minimum), driven through the real tool registry wherever the behaviour is model-facing. The supervisor reviews the test list against this spec and rejects under-tested work. In your completion notes, map each TESTS bullet to the test name that covers it.

NOTE: migrations 0032-0035 already exist on your branch, so 0036 is correct. The importer regeneration also rewrites any generated inventory docs (docs/inventories/*semi-structured-boundary*) — regenerate them through their script if verify flags them stale (the use-an-object child had to). Encounter combatants now carry death_rules/dying/stable and recovery columns (0033): when head_count reaches 0, the creature "dies" — use status 'dead' through updateCombatant so concentration/actor sync run. updateCombatant now validates explicit statuses: 'dead' is always allowed.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation per the description on its own branch; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
notes:
Dispatched gpt-6-luna high, pgid 2635536, off eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8@23ea3385.
Completed in commit 9d066ddb on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6.1.

Files changed: curated the source-pinned Multiple Heads mechanic and kind validation; regenerated Hydra records and semi-structured boundary inventory; added migration 0036 and schema snapshot; implemented tracked head initialization, per-turn damage threshold, death, fire suppression, end-turn regrowth/healing, reaction derivation, and model-facing head counts; updated tool/protocol/context/docs and migration, importer, and engine tests.

Decisions/deviations: implemented the supervisor decisions without deviation. Source scan found the ettin Two Heads trait but it lacks the Multiple Heads loss/regrowth lifecycle, so the mechanic applies only to the Hydra. No follow-up issue was discovered.

TESTS mapping:
- Importer mechanic values, source span/provenance, kind schema acceptance and invalid-value rejection: Multiple Heads curated source mechanic / projects the source-backed values and provenance on the real Hydra trait.
- Initial five heads, 24 damage without loss, 25 accumulated across two hits, and at most one head per turn: initializes head count and applies the 24/25 single-turn threshold once.
- Threshold reset on the next structured turn: resets the damage threshold on the next structured turn.
- Fire suppression: fire damage suppresses regrowth at the end of the creature's turn.
- Two heads regrow per dead head and 10 HP per regrown head: regrows two heads per dead head and heals 10 HP for each regrown head.
- Zero heads means dead: sets a tracked multi-head creature dead when its final head dies.
- Derived allowance tracks five heads and preserves opportunity-attack restriction; allowance updates after head loss: derives hydra reaction allowance from tracked heads and preserves the restriction; initializes head count and applies the 24/25 single-turn threshold once.
- Model-supplied reactionAllowance rejected: rejects a model-supplied reaction allowance argument.
- Creature without Multiple Heads remains at one reaction and untracked: leaves creatures without Multiple Heads on the ordinary one-reaction budget.
- Roster/context exposes head count: derives hydra reaction allowance from tracked heads and preserves the restriction.

Evidence: npm run verify:worktree passed (320 test files passed, 2 skipped; 5,650 tests passed, 3 skipped; check and typecheck green). npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack passed byte-for-byte (records changed 0; source PDF SHA-256 2504d2a0abb0a4d491a939be4f17910a2dde0312570ab8d208080225ccf0a1f0). npm run audit:rules-pack reported zero suspicious records.
